pass_a_gloss: you have trained, but so that you may be revealed. Do not become unrighteous, nor godless. These we remember in the times of the surrounding circumstances, and we hear the glory of God present and speaking to us: Do you think I have [something] for you, or so that the righteousness of you becomes clear to the ignorant? 5. Take up height and power, put on glory and honor. Crown yourself, put on glory, put on something, put on beauty. The insolent has been defeated against you; you have humbled the proud, and you have turned his armies far away with shame. –Rebuke sinners, showing them to be sinners; fill their faces with dishonor, through the rebuke within you. –Not indeed for display or for all the rest, or even for god-knowledge. See how much the lowly nature rebukes him, and he does not say that you are lowly, but that I am great, and he cannot do whatever I do. 9. But behold, beasts are against you. As an athlete, learn the things about the opponent's act. –Indeed, says, against you, and against all the patient ones these beasts are made to cease and are subjected; there is yet [etc]. 10. You will lead a dragon in a hook, and you will put a bridle around his nose? Can you, says, O Job, do what the Only-begotten did later? Just as a thing, he projected his own flesh through his own ribs, as through hooks, he drew up Leviathan. Thus the Hebrew has it, and it means the dragon. 387 k. You will lay your hand on him, remembering the war being in his body [and no longer being]? War he says is the disturbance, the wildness, his being embittered. How does it happen, says? Such is a wild and powerful and unmanageable beast. Can you, says, by your power subdue him? Or at all to remember and conceive the war about to be in his body? His body he says is demons, as being his head; this war the Lord conquered through the trophy of the cross. –But the [word] 'no longer be' because once the cross has been. For he who died to sin, says, died once. Chap. MA, 4. Who will reveal the face of his clothing? The
pass_b_english: You have undergone training, not merely for the sake of discipline, but so that you might be revealed. Do not allow yourself to appear unrighteous or godless. We must hold these truths in mind during times of surrounding trials, hearing the glory of God present and speaking to us: 'Do you suppose I have used you for any other purpose than so that your own righteousness might be made manifest to those who are ignorant?'

Therefore, take up height and power; clothe yourself in glory and honor. Crown yourself, don splendor, and put on true beauty. The insolent man has been defeated by your presence; you have humbled the proud and driven his phalanxes far away in shame. Rebuke sinners by exposing their sinfulness, filling their faces with dishonor through the rebuke that resides within you. This is not done for mere display or for any other worldly end, but even for the knowledge of God. Observe how much the lowly nature of the creature rebukes him; he does not say that you are lowly, but rather, 'I am great, and I cannot do what you do.'

But behold, beasts are set against you. Like an athlete, learn the tactics of your opponent's movements. These beasts are set against you and against all who are patient, yet they are eventually subdued and brought to heel. Will you draw a dragon with a hook and put a bridle upon his nose? Can you, O Job, do what the Only-begotten later accomplished? Just as one might catch a fish by projecting his own flesh through his own ribs like hooks, so did Leviathan draw up the dragon; thus the Hebrew text signifies the dragon. You will lay your hand upon him, remembering the war that occurs within his body—a war that shall be no more. This 'war' refers to the disturbance, the wildness, and the embittered state of the beast. How does it happen? It is a wild, powerful, and unmanageable beast. Can you, by your own strength, bind him? Or can you even conceive of the war that is to take place within his own body? He calls the body 'demons,' as if they were his head; yet the Lord conquered this war through the trophy of the cross. The phrase 'let it be no more' exists because once the cross has been established, he who died to sin has died once for all [[Hebrews 9:28 >> Bible:Hebrews 9:28]]. Who, then, will reveal the face of his clothing?
